newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Trade Ministry denies tortilla price hike.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Trade Ministry denies tortilla price hike.

text.p: Mexico's Trade Ministry denied Wednesday it had agreed to an April increase in the price of corn pancake tortillas.
"It is not true that prices are going to be increased, it is not on the cards," Javier Herrera, a spokesman for the Trade Ministry, told Reuters.
A radio report said earlier Wednesday that the government had agreed to hike prices to 2.50 pesos per kilo of tortillas in Mexico City from 1.70 peso per kilo starting in April.
The National Corn Flour and Tortilla Producers Chamber has been pressing the government for several weeks to raise prices or lift price controls, claiming prices do not cover production costs.

Tortillas, corn flour pancakes eaten more widely than bread, have an important weighting in the consumer price index. The food is highly politicised and one of the last remaining basics still under strict price controls in Mexico.
